def test_cli_round_preserves_pipeline_precision(tmp_path, capsys):
    # CLI Issue 4: intermediate sort does not corrupt full precision for later agg
    df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["x", "x"], "v": [0.4, 0.4]})
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)
    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-round", "0", "-arrange", "v", "-by", "g", "-agg", "sum"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "1" in out


def test_cli_repeated_flags_run_with_respective_values(tmp_path, capsys):
    # CLI Issue 7: -head 1 -head 3 runs head 1 then head 3 (result has 1 row)
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": range(10)})
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)
    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-head", "1", "-head", "3", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(1, 1)"


def test_cli_expand_paths_literal_bracket_file(tmp_path, capsys):
    # CLI Issue 9: data[1].csv read literally when file exists
    p = tmp_path / "data[1].csv"
    p.write_text("a,b\n1,2\n")
    exit_code = cli.main([str(p), "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(1, 2)"


def test_cli_time_single_and_multi_runs(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3], "b": [4, 5, 6]})
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    # 1. Bare -time (1 run)
    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-shape", "-time"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    lines = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert len(lines) == 2
    assert lines[0] == "(3, 2)"
    assert lines[1].startswith("Elapsed (1 run): ") and " ms" in lines[1]

    # 2. Bare -time before path
    exit_code2 = cli.main(["-time", path, "-shape"])
    assert exit_code2 == 0
    out2 = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "(3, 2)" in out2
    assert "Elapsed (1 run): " in out2

    # 3. -time 5 (5 runs, output emitted once)
    exit_code5 = cli.main([path, "-shape", "-time", "5"])
    assert exit_code5 == 0
    lines5 = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert len(lines5) == 2
    assert lines5[0] == "(3, 2)"
    assert lines5[1].startswith("Elapsed (5 runs): avg ")
    assert " | min " in lines5[1] and " | max " in lines5[1] and " | total " in lines5[1]

    # 4. Invalid -time 0
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc:
        cli.main([path, "-shape", "-time", "0"])
    assert exc.value.code == 2
    assert "must be > 0" in capsys.readouterr().err

    # 5. -h time
    exit_help = cli.main(["-h", "time"])
    assert exit_help == 0
    assert "PYTAE CLI KEYWORD HELP: -time" in capsys.readouterr().out

import os

def test_join_on_differing_column_names(tmp_path, capsys):
    left, right = _write_two_csvs(tmp_path)

    cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{left}=df1;{right}=df2",
            "-join",
            "left=df1,right=df2,on=col a:cola",
        ]
    )

    out = capsys.readouterr().out.strip()
    assert "val_l" in out and "val_r" in out
    assert len(out.splitlines()) == 3  # header + 2 matching rows (inner join)


def test_join_on_pair_quoting_is_optional(tmp_path, capsys):

    cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{left}=df1;{right}=df2",
            "-join",
            "left=df1,right=df2,on=col a:'cola'",
        ]
    )

    out = capsys.readouterr().out.strip()
    assert "val_l" in out and "val_r" in out
    assert len(out.splitlines()) == 3


def test_join_shared_column_name_outer_join(tmp_path, capsys):
    left = tmp_path / "a.csv"
    right = tmp_path / "b.csv"
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "x": ["a", "b", "c"]}).to_csv(left, index=False)
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 4], "y": ["p", "q", "r"]}).to_csv(right, index=False)

    cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{left}=a;{right}=b",

def test_concat_resets_index(tmp_path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    a, b, _ = _write_three_id_csvs(tmp_path)
    copied = {}

    def _fake_to_clipboard(self, *args, **kwargs):
        copied["frame"] = self.copy()

    monkeypatch.setattr(pd.DataFrame, "to_clipboard", _fake_to_clipboard)

    cli.main(["-file", f"{a}=a;{b}=b", "-concat", "frames='a,b'", "-o", "clip"])

    result = copied["frame"]
    assert list(result.index) == list(range(len(result)))

def test_file_dlim_and_encoding_overrides_applied(tmp_path, capsys):
    pipe_path = tmp_path / "pipe.csv"
    pipe_path.write_bytes("id|name\n1|caf\xe9\n".encode("latin-1"))
    plain_path = tmp_path / "plain.csv"
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [2], "name": ["bravo"]}).to_csv(plain_path, index=False)

    cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{pipe_path}=p,dlim=|,encoding=latin-1; {plain_path}=q",
            "-concat",
            "frames='p,q'",
        ]
    )

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "café" in out
    assert "bravo" in out

def test_join_validate_failure_errors(tmp_path, capsys):
    left = tmp_path / "left.csv"
    right = tmp_path / "right.csv"
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 1, 2], "x": ["a", "b", "c"]}).to_csv(left, index=False)
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "y": ["p", "q"]}).to_csv(right, index=False)

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main(
            [
                "-file",
                f"{left}=l;{right}=r",
                "-join",
                "left=l,right=r,on=id,validate=one_to_one",
            ]
        )
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    assert "-join:" in capsys.readouterr().err


def test_output_succeeds_after_join(tmp_path):
    left, right = _write_two_csvs(tmp_path)
    dest = tmp_path / "joined.parquet"

    exit_code = cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{left}=df1;{right}=df2",
            "-join",
            "left=df1,right=df2,on=col a:cola",
            "-o",
            str(dest),
        ]
    )

    assert exit_code == 0
    assert dest.exists()
    result = pd.read_parquet(dest)
    assert list(result.columns) == ["col a", "val_l", "cola", "val_r"]
    assert len(result) == 2


def test_file_nonexistent_path_errors(tmp_path, capsys):
    a, _, _ = _write_three_id_csvs(tmp_path)

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main(["-file", f"{a}=a;{tmp_path / 'missing.csv'}=b", "-concat", "frames='a,b'"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    assert "file not found" in capsys.readouterr().err


def test_file_bad_encoding_errors(tmp_path, capsys):
    bad_path = tmp_path / "bad.csv"
    bad_path.write_bytes("id,name\n1,caf\xe9\n".encode("latin-1"))
    ok_path = tmp_path / "ok.csv"
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [2], "name": ["bravo"]}).to_csv(ok_path, index=False)

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main(["-file", f"{bad_path}=a;{ok_path}=b", "-concat", "frames='a,b'"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    assert "try -encoding" in capsys.readouterr().err


def test_concat_unquoted_frames(tmp_path, capsys):
    a, b, c = _write_three_id_csvs(tmp_path)

    # unquoted frames=a,b,c without inner quotes
    exit_code = cli.main(["-file", f"{a}=a;{b}=b;{c}=c", "-concat", "frames=a,b,c", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(8, 4)"


def test_join_unquoted_on_pairs(tmp_path, capsys):
    left = tmp_path / "l.csv"
    right = tmp_path / "r.csv"
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "code": ["x", "y"], "v1": [10, 20]}).to_csv(left, index=False)
    pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "code": ["x", "y"], "v2": [100, 200]}).to_csv(right, index=False)

    exit_code = cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{left}=df1;{right}=df2",
            "-join",
            "left=df1,right=df2,on=id:id,code:code",
            "-shape",
        ]
    )
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(2, 4)"


def test_join_df_alias_rejected(tmp_path, capsys):
    a, b, _ = _write_three_id_csvs(tmp_path)
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main(
            [
                "-file",
                f"{a}=a;{b}=b",
                "-join",
                "left=a,right=b,on=id",
                "-join",
                "left=df,right=b,on=id",
            ]
        )
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    assert "'df' is not a valid alias; use 'data' for the pipeline's current result" in capsys.readouterr().err

import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

from pytae import cli
from tests.cli_helpers import _write_csv


def test_mutate_then_select_new_column(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(
        tmp_path,
        pd.DataFrame({"body_mass_g": [3000.0, 4000.0], "bill_length_mm": [30.0, 40.0]}),
    )

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-mutate", "bmi = body_mass_g / bill_length_mm ** 2", "-select", "bmi", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(2, 1)"


def test_mutate_multiple_entries_and_chained_reference(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"body_mass_g": [3000.0, 4000.0]}))

    cli.main(
        [
            path,
            "-mutate",
            "mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000, mass_lb = mass_kg * 2.20462",
            "-select",
            "mass_kg,mass_lb",
            "-head",
        ]
    )
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "mass_kg" in out and "mass_lb" in out


def test_mutate_key_quoting_is_optional(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"body_mass_g": [3000.0, 4000.0]}))

    cli.main([path, "-mutate", "mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000", "-select", "mass_kg", "-shape"])
    unquoted = capsys.readouterr().out.strip()

    cli.main([path, "-mutate", "'mass_kg' = body_mass_g / 1000", "-select", "mass_kg", "-shape"])
    quoted = capsys.readouterr().out.strip()

    assert unquoted == quoted == "(2, 1)"


def test_mutate_unknown_column_reference_errors(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"body_mass_g": [3000.0, 4000.0]}))

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main([path, "-mutate", "bmi = bod_mass_g / 1000", "-shape"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "-mutate" in err
    assert "body_mass_g" in err

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main([path, "-mutate", "heavy = n >= @threshold"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "-mutate" in err
    assert "library-only" in err


def test_mutate_at_inside_quoted_string_is_not_flagged_as_local_var(tmp_path, capsys):

# FILE: tests/test_cli_new_features.py
################################################################################
import io
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import pytest

from pytae.cli import main

PENGUINS_PATH = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "src" / "pytae" / "datasets" / "penguins.parquet")


def test_cli_glimpse(capsys):
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-glimpse"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "Rows: 344" in captured.out
    assert "Columns: 7" in captured.out
    assert "$ species" in captured.out
    assert "$ body_mass_g" in captured.out


def test_cli_dropna_bare_default_zero_data_loss(capsys):
    # Option B: Bare -dropna defaults to how='all' (preserves all rows unless a row is 100% null)
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-dropna", "-shape"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "(344, 7)" in captured.out


def test_cli_dropna_how_any(capsys):
    # Explicit how=any drops rows with any missing value (344 -> 333)
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-dropna", "how=any", "-shape"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "(333, 7)" in captured.out


def test_cli_drop_nulls_alias(capsys):
    # -drop_nulls is an alias for -dropna
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-drop_nulls", "-shape"])
    assert ret == 0
    assert "(344, 7)" in capsys.readouterr().out

    ret2 = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-drop_nulls", "how=any", "-shape"])
    assert ret2 == 0
    assert "(333, 7)" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_cli_drop_na_alias(capsys):
    # -drop_na is also an alias for -dropna
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-drop_na", "-shape"])
    assert ret == 0
    assert "(344, 7)" in capsys.readouterr().out


def test_cli_dropna_specific_columns(capsys):
    # Dropping rows with missing body_mass_g reduces rows from 344 to 342
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-dropna", "body_mass_g", "-shape"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "(342, 7)" in captured.out


def test_cli_dropna_chained_with_agg(capsys):
    ret = main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-dropna", "body_mass_g", "-by", "species", "-agg", "count=n"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "Adelie    151" in captured.out
    assert "Gentoo    123" in captured.out


def test_cli_dropna_unknown_column(capsys):
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        main([PENGUINS_PATH, "-dropna", "nonexistent_col"])
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "Column 'nonexistent_col' does not exist" in captured.err or "unknown column" in captured.err.lower()


def test_cli_auto_pipe_detection(monkeypatch, capsys):
    # Simulate piped stdin
    csv_data = b"col1,col2\n10,20\n30,40\n"
    fake_stdin = io.BytesIO(csv_data)
    fake_stdin.buffer = fake_stdin

    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, "stdin", fake_stdin)
    monkeypatch.setattr(fake_stdin, "isatty", lambda: False)

    # Call main without specifying any path
    ret = main(["-head", "2"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "col1" in captured.out
    assert "10" in captured.out


def test_cli_clipboard_ingestion(monkeypatch, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"fruit": ["apple", "banana"], "price": [1.5, 2.0]})
    monkeypatch.setattr(pd, "read_clipboard", lambda **kwargs: df.copy())

    # Test pytae clip
    ret = main(["clip", "-head", "2"])
    assert ret == 0
    captured = capsys.readouterr()
    assert "apple" in captured.out
    assert "banana" in captured.out

    # pytae from_clip and pytae clipboard are not recognized as clipboard
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        main(["from_clip", "-shape"])

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        main(["clipboard", "-shape"])

# FILE: tests/test_cli_parse.py

import os
import sys

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))


def test_parse_sort_by_trailing_direction():
    from pytae.cli_parsing import parse_sort_by

    assert parse_sort_by("val") == (["val"], "asc")
    assert parse_sort_by("val desc") == (["val"], "desc")
    assert parse_sort_by("species,body_mass_g desc") == (["species", "body_mass_g"], "desc")
    assert parse_sort_by("bill length mm desc") == (["bill length mm"], "desc")


def test_expand_paths_single_and_list(tmp_path):
    import pytest

    from pytae.cli_parsing import expand_paths

    f1 = tmp_path / "a.csv"
    f2 = tmp_path / "b.csv"
    f1.write_text("a,b\n1,2\n")
    f2.write_text("a,b\n3,4\n")

    assert expand_paths(str(f1)) == [f1]
    assert expand_paths([str(f1), str(f2)]) == [f1, f2]
    assert expand_paths(str(tmp_path / "*.csv")) == [f1, f2]
    assert expand_paths([str(f1), str(f1), str(f2)]) == [f1, f2]

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        expand_paths(str(tmp_path / "*.parquet"))
    assert "no files matched pattern" in str(exc_info.value)


def test_parse_rename_conflicting_mappings():
    import pytest

    from pytae.cli_parsing import parse_rename

    assert parse_rename("old:new, other:target") == {"old": "new", "other": "target"}
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        parse_rename("col:new1, col:new2")
    assert "conflicting mappings for 'col'" in str(exc_info.value)


def test_cli_keyword_help(capsys):
    from pytae.cli import main

    # test `pytae -help sql`
    code = main(["-help", "sql"])
    assert code == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "PYTAE CLI KEYWORD HELP: -sql" in out
    assert "FLAG:     -sql, --sql QUERY" in out
    assert "select species" in out

    # test `pytae -h mutate`
    code = main(["-h", "mutate"])
    assert code == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "PYTAE CLI KEYWORD HELP: -mutate" in out
    assert "mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000" in out

    # test unknown keyword fallback
    code = main(["-help", "nonexistent_keyword"])
    assert code == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "No dedicated help topic for keyword 'nonexistent_keyword'" in out
    assert "Available keywords with help:" in out

    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols == ["Region", "avg_sales", "count"]


def test_cli_pivot_rich_metrics_2d_unquoted(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "West"],
            "Year": [2020, 2021, 2020],
            "Sales": [100.0, 200.0, 300.0],
        }
    )
    p = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region, c=Year, v=rev=Sales:sum, count=n", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols == ["Region", "rev_2020", "rev_2021", "orders_2020", "orders_2021"] or cols == [
        "Region",
        "rev_2020",
        "rev_2021",
        "count_2020",
        "count_2021",
    ]


def test_cli_pivot_multi_func(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "West"],
            "Sales": [100.0, 200.0, 300.0],
        }
    )
    p = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region, v=Sales:[mean, sum]", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols == ["Region", "Sales_mean", "Sales_sum"]


def test_cli_pivot_optional_v(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "West"],
            "Year": [2020, 2021, 2020],
            "Store": ["S1", "S2", "S1"],
        }
    )
    p = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    # 2D table without v
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region, c=Year", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols == ["Region", "2020", "2021"]

    # 1D row frequency table without v
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region,Store", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols == ["Region", "Store", "n"]


def test_cli_pivot_f_v(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "Region": ["East", "East", "West"],
            "Quarter": ["Q1", "Q1", "Q2"],
            "Sales": [100.0, 200.0, 300.0],
        }
    )
    p = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    # f_v=0 works
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region, c=Quarter, v=Sales, a=sum, f_v=0", "-head"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    out_fv = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "East" in out_fv

    # fill=0 is rejected
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region, c=Quarter, v=Sales, fill=0"])

    # fill_value=0 is rejected
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit):
        cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=Region, c=Quarter, v=Sales, fill_value=0"])


def test_cli_pivot_single_metric_2d_no_prefix(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "cola": ["A1", "A2"],
            "colb": ["B1", "B2"],
            "colc": ["C1", "C2"],
            "colv": [10.0, 20.0],
        }
    )
    p = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)
    # pytae x.parquet -pivot "r=cola,colb,c=colc,v=colv:sum"
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=cola,colb,c=colc,v=colv:sum", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols == ["cola", "colb", "C1", "C2"]


def test_cli_pivot_default_f_v_is_null_for_metrics(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "island": ["Torgersen", "Biscoe"],
            "sex": ["male", "female"],
            "mass": [100.0, 200.0],
        }
    )
    p = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)
    exit_code = cli.main([p, "-pivot", "r=island,c=sex,v=mass:sum"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "NaN" in out or "null" in out

# FILE: tests/test_cli_sample_datasets.py
################################################################################
"""Integration tests against pytae's bundled real datasets (pytae.sample_data).

Unlike the tiny hand-crafted frames in test_cli_order.py (kept deliberately
minimal for exact, easy-to-verify assertions), these exercise the CLI against
real, messier data: multiple categories, real NaNs, larger row counts. This is
also where docs/pytae.md's "Sample datasets" section examples are regression
tested, so a broken documented command fails CI instead of only being caught
by manually re-running the docs.
"""

import os
import sys

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

from pytae import cli

_SAMPLE_DATASET_NAMES = ("penguins", "tips", "titanic", "diamonds", "mpg", "flights")


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def sample_dataset_dir(tmp_path_factory):
    """Write every bundled sample dataset to parquet once, shared across this module's tests."""
    import pytae

    directory = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("sample_datasets")
    for name in _SAMPLE_DATASET_NAMES:
        pytae.sample_data[name].to_parquet(directory / f"{name}.parquet")
    return directory


# Mirrors docs/pytae.md's "Sample datasets" section — keep in sync with those examples.
_DOC_EXAMPLES = [
    ("penguins.parquet", ["-filter", "species = 'Adelie'", "-by", "species", "-agg", "mean"]),
    ("penguins.parquet", ["-pivot", "r=species,c=island,v=sex,a=n"]),
    ("tips.parquet", ["-select", "day,total_bill,tip", "-by", "day", "-mutate", "avg_tip = mean(tip)"]),
    ("titanic.parquet", ["-freq", "survived"]),
    ("diamonds.parquet", ["-select", "cut,price", "-by", "cut", "-agg", "mean"]),
    ("mpg.parquet", ["-select", "origin,mpg", "-arrange", "mpg desc", "-head", "5"]),
    ("flights.parquet", ["-wide", "c=month,v=passengers,r=year", "-head", "5"]),
]


@pytest.mark.parametrize("filename, extra_args", _DOC_EXAMPLES)
def test_docs_sample_dataset_examples_run_cleanly(sample_dataset_dir, filename, extra_args, capsys):
    exit_code = cli.main([str(sample_dataset_dir / filename), *extra_args])
    assert exit_code == 0, capsys.readouterr().err


def test_pivot_a_n_counts_on_real_penguins(sample_parquet, capsys):
    path = sample_parquet("penguins")

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-pivot", "r=species,c=island,v=sex,a=n"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    wide_out = capsys.readouterr().out

    def _row(line):
        return [int(tok) for tok in line.split()[1:]]

    wide_rows = {line.split()[0]: _row(line) for line in wide_out.strip().splitlines()[1:]}
    assert wide_rows["Adelie"] == [44, 56, 52]
    assert wide_rows["Chinstrap"] == [0, 68, 0]
    assert wide_rows["Gentoo"] == [124, 0, 0]


def test_wide_pure_reshape_on_real_flights(sample_parquet, capsys):
    path = sample_parquet("flights")

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-wide", "c=month,v=passengers,r=year", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    cols = capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines()
    assert cols[0] == "year"
    assert "Jan" in cols
    assert "Dec" in cols


def test_agg_groups_by_diamonds_cut_categories(sample_parquet, capsys):
    path = sample_parquet("diamonds")

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "cut,price", "-by", "cut", "-agg", "mean", "-shape"])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert out.strip() == "(5, 2)"  # 5 known cut categories: Fair/Good/Very Good/Premium/Ideal


def test_group_by_agg_sum_matches_known_flights_totals(sample_parquet, capsys):
    path = sample_parquet("flights")

    exit_code = cli.main(
        [
            path,
            "-by",
            "year",
            "-agg",
            "passengers = sum",
            "-head",
            "3",
        ]
    )

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    rows = [line.split() for line in out.strip().splitlines()[1:]]
    assert rows == [["1949", "1520"], ["1950", "1676"], ["1951", "2042"]]


def test_handle_missing_fills_real_titanic_nans(sample_parquet, capsys):
    # titanic has genuine NaNs in numeric (age) and object (deck) columns.
    path = sample_parquet("titanic")

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-handle_missing", "-select", "age,deck", "-nulls"])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert out.strip().splitlines() == ["age     0", "deck    0"]

# FILE: tests/test_cli_select.py

import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

from pytae import cli
from tests.cli_helpers import _write_csv, _write_two_csvs


def test_select_regex_matches_column_names(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["A", "B"],
            "bill_length_mm": [1, 2],
            "bill_depth_mm": [3, 4],
            "body_mass_g": [5, 6],
        }
    )
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "regex=^bill", "-cols"])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert out.strip().splitlines() == ["bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm"]


def test_select_regex_combines_with_explicit_select(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["A"],
            "island": ["Torgersen"],
            "bill_length_mm": [1],
            "body_mass_g": [2],
        }
    )
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "species,regex=bill|body", "-cols"])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert out.strip().splitlines() == ["species", "bill_length_mm", "body_mass_g"]


def test_parse_select_spec_names_and_kwargs():
    names, kwargs = cli.parse_select_spec("species,contains=bill,dtype=numeric")
    assert names == ["species"]
    assert kwargs == {"contains": "bill", "dtype": "numeric"}


def test_parse_select_spec_quoted_name_and_repeated_key():
    names, kwargs = cli.parse_select_spec("'bill length mm',contains=bill,contains=body")
    assert names == ["bill length mm"]
    assert kwargs == {"contains": ["bill", "body"]}


def test_select_dtype_unions_with_explicit_names(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"cola": ["a"], "colb": [1], "n": [2.0], "label": ["x"]})
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "cola,colb,dtype=numeric", "-cols"])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert out.strip().splitlines() == ["cola", "colb", "n"]


def test_select_exclude_dtype_standalone(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"name": ["a"], "n": [1]}))

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "exclude_dtype=numeric", "-cols"])

    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["name"]


def test_select_exclude_dtype_non_numeric_keeps_numbers(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"name": ["a"], "n": [1], "x": [2.0]}))

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "exclude_dtype=non_numeric", "-cols"])

    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["n", "x"]


def test_select_exclude_dtype_cannot_combine(tmp_path):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"name": ["a"], "n": [1]}))

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="exclude_dtype cannot be combined"):
        cli.main([path, "-select", "name,exclude_dtype=numeric", "-cols"])


def test_select_slice(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": [3], "d": [4]})
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "a:c", "-cols"])

    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["a", "b", "c"]


def test_second_select_filters_remaining_names(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": [3], "d": [4]}))

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "a,b,c", "-select", "a,c", "-cols"])

    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["a", "c"]


def test_second_select_rejects_name_not_kept_by_first(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": [3]}))

    # last-wins would yield b,c; chaining rejects c because the first spec dropped it
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main([path, "-select", "a,b", "-select", "b,c", "-cols"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "unknown column" in err
    assert "'c'" in err


def test_select_only_prints_selected_table(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": [3]}))

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "a,b"])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert "a" in out and "b" in out
    assert "c" not in out.split()


def test_select_unknown_exact_name_errors(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"a": [1], "b": [2], "c": [3]}))

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main([path, "-select", "d,a,b", "-cols"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2
    err = capsys.readouterr().err
    assert "unknown column" in err
    assert "'d'" in err


def test_select_after_agg_df_sees_agg_columns(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(
        tmp_path,
        pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["x", "x", "y"], "val": [1, 2, 3], "z": [9, 8, 7]}),
    )

    # n is created by agg; a starting-view -select would reject it
    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-by", "grp", "-agg", "val = sum, n = n", "-select", "grp,n", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["grp", "n"]


def test_select_agg_df_select_shape_chains(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(
        tmp_path,
        pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["x", "x", "y"], "val": [1, 2, 3], "z": [9, 8, 7]}),
    )

    # starting-view chaining would collapse to val-only before agg → (1, 1)
    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "grp,val", "-by", "grp", "-agg", "sum", "-select", "val", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(2, 1)"


def test_second_select_intersects_dtype_and_contains(tmp_path, capsys):
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["A"],
            "bill_length_mm": [1],
            "bill_depth_mm": [2],
            "body_mass_g": [3],
            "island": ["Torgersen"],
        }
    )
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, df)

    # last-wins of dtype=numeric would keep body_mass_g too
    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "contains=bill", "-select", "dtype=numeric", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm"]

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-select", "dtype=numeric", "-select", "contains=bill", "-cols"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip().splitlines() == ["bill_length_mm", "bill_depth_mm"]


def test_removed_select_star_flags_are_unknown(tmp_path):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]}))

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main([path, "-select-regex", "^a", "-cols"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2


def test_select_caret_pattern_is_not_implicit_regex(tmp_path):

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:
        cli.main([path, "-select", "^bill", "-cols"])
    assert exc_info.value.code == 2


def test_select_then_filter_on_dropped_column_errors(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(
        tmp_path,
        pd.DataFrame({"keep": [1, 2], "flt": ["A", "B"], "val": [10, 20]}),
    )

    with pytest.raises(SystemExit) as exc_info:

def test_select_runs_after_join(tmp_path, capsys):
    left, right = _write_two_csvs(tmp_path)

    cli.main(
        [
            "-file",
            f"{left}=df1;{right}=df2",
            "-join",
            "left=df1,right=df2,on=col a:cola",
            "-select",
            "val_l,val_r",
            "-shape",
        ]
    )

    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(2, 2)"

# FILE: tests/test_cli_sql.py
################################################################################
import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

from pytae import cli
from tests.cli_helpers import _write_csv, _write_two_csvs


def test_sql_query_via_data_alias(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"col a": [1, 20, 3], "col b": ["x", "y", "z"]}))

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-sql", 'select "col b" from data where "col a" > 10'])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert "y" in out
    assert "x" not in out


def test_sql_spaced_column_name_needs_double_quotes(tmp_path, capsys):
    # Standard SQL identifier quoting: double quotes for names with spaces, not single quotes.
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"bill length mm": [1, 20, 3], "species": ["a", "b", "c"]}))

    exit_code = cli.main([path, "-sql", 'select species from data where "bill length mm" > 10'])

    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert out.strip().splitlines()[-1].strip() == "b"


def test_sql_only_data_is_registered_no_file_derived_alias(tmp_path, capsys):

def test_sql_load_from_file_cli(tmp_path, capsys):

    qfile = tmp_path / "query.txt"
    qfile.write_text("select a, b from data where a > 1")

    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(1, 2)"


def test_sql_load_from_quoted_file_cli(tmp_path, capsys):
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": [10, 20]}))
    sub = tmp_path / "subdir"
    sub.mkdir()
    qfile = sub / "query.txt"
    qfile.write_text("select a, b from data where a > 1")

    # Test with outer quotes around '@path'
    exit_code = cli.main([str(path), "-sql", f"'@{qfile}'", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(1, 2)"

    # Test with quotes around the path itself '@"path"'
    exit_code = cli.main([str(path), "-sql", f'@"{qfile}"', "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(1, 2)"

    exit_code = cli.main([str(path), "-sql", "select [col a], `col b` from data", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(2, 2)"


def test_cli_sql_works_without_duckdb(tmp_path, capsys, monkeypatch):
    import builtins

    real_import = builtins.__import__

    def blocked(name, *args, **kwargs):
        if name == "duckdb" or name.startswith("duckdb."):
            raise ImportError("duckdb is not installed")
        return real_import(name, *args, **kwargs)

    monkeypatch.setattr(builtins, "__import__", blocked)
    path = _write_csv(tmp_path, pd.DataFrame({"x": [10, 20, 30], "y": ["a", "b", "c"]}))
    exit_code = cli.main([str(path), "-sql", "select y from data where x >= 20", "-shape"])
    assert exit_code == 0
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "(2, 1)"

# FILE: tests/test_fillna.py
################################################################################
from __future__ import annotations

import math

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl
import pytest

import pytae as pt


def test_df_fillna_scalar_default_nans_true():
    # Both NaN and null are filled by default
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
        "txt": ["a", None, "c"],
        "num": [10, None, 30],
    })
    res = df.fillna(0.0)
    assert res["flt"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    # String column untouched because 0.0 is float
    assert res["txt"].to_list() == ["a", None, "c"]
    assert res["num"].to_list() == [10.0, 0.0, 30.0]


def test_df_fillna_scalar_nans_false():
    # Only null is filled; NaN remains intact
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
        "txt": ["a", None, "c"],
    })
    res = df.fillna(0.0, nans=False)
    flt_vals = res["flt"].to_list()
    assert flt_vals[0] == 1.0
    assert math.isnan(flt_vals[1])
    assert flt_vals[2] == 0.0


def test_df_fillna_dict():
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
        "txt": ["a", None, "c"],
        "num": [10, None, 30],
    })
    res = df.fillna({"flt": -1.0, "txt": "MISSING", "num": 0})
    assert res["flt"].to_list() == [1.0, -1.0, -1.0]
    assert res["txt"].to_list() == ["a", "MISSING", "c"]
    assert res["num"].to_list() == [10, 0, 30]


def test_df_fillna_subset_and_cols():
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "flt1": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
        "flt2": [2.0, float("nan"), None],
    })
    # Target flt1 only via *cols
    r1 = df.fillna(0.0, "flt1")
    assert r1["flt1"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    assert math.isnan(r1["flt2"].to_list()[1])
    assert r1["flt2"].to_list()[2] is None

    # Target flt2 only via subset=
    r2 = df.fillna(99.0, subset=["flt2"])
    assert r2["flt2"].to_list() == [2.0, 99.0, 99.0]
    assert math.isnan(r2["flt1"].to_list()[1])


def test_df_fillna_missing_column_raises_key_error():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="fillna: column\\(s\\) \\['non_existent'\\] not found"):
        df.fillna(0, "non_existent")


def test_df_fillna_missing_value_raises_type_error():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2, 3]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="fillna\\(\\) missing required argument: 'value'"):
        df.fillna()


def test_df_fill_null_and_fill_nan():
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
    })
    # fill_null fills null only (nans=False)
    r_null = df.fill_null(0.0)
    assert math.isnan(r_null["flt"].to_list()[1])
    assert r_null["flt"].to_list()[2] == 0.0

    # fill_nan fills NaN only, leaving null intact
    r_nan = df.fill_nan(0.0)
    assert r_nan["flt"].to_list()[0] == 1.0
    assert r_nan["flt"].to_list()[1] == 0.0
    assert r_nan["flt"].to_list()[2] is None


def test_functional_and_accessor_fillna():
    # 1. Polars accessor
    pldf = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, float("nan"), None]})
    res_pl = pldf.pt.fillna(0.0)
    assert isinstance(res_pl, pt.DataFrame)
    assert res_pl["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 2. Pandas accessor
    pddf = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, float("nan"), None]})
    res_pd = pddf.pt.fillna(0.0)
    assert isinstance(res_pd, pt.DataFrame)
    assert res_pd["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 3. Top-level pt.fillna
    res_fn = pt.fillna(pldf, 5.0)
    assert res_fn["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 5.0, 5.0]


def test_grouped_dataframe_fillna():
    df = pt.DataFrame({
        "grp": ["A", "A", "B", "B"],
        "val": [1.0, float("nan"), None, 4.0],
    })
    res = df.by("grp").fillna(0.0)
    assert res["val"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 4.0]

# FILE: tests/test_import.py

import os
import subprocess
import sys

_SRC = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src"))


def test_import_does_not_load_plotting_shape_or_samples():
    code = (
        r"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, %r)
import pytae

assert "pytae.plotting" not in sys.modules
assert "pytae.shape" not in sys.modules
assert "matplotlib" not in sys.modules
assert "duckdb" not in sys.modules
assert pytae._cache == {}
assert "penguins" in pytae.sample_data
assert list(pytae.sample_data.keys())
assert pytae._cache == {}

# keys() returns a plain readable tuple, not a bare KeysView object
keys = pytae.sample_data.keys()
assert isinstance(keys, tuple)
assert "penguins" in keys

df = pytae.sample("penguins")
assert len(df) > 0
# sample() returns a copy each time, so mutating it never poisons the cache
assert pytae.sample_data["penguins"] is not df
df.iloc[0, 0] = "MUTATED"
assert pytae.sample_data["penguins"].iloc[0, 0] != "MUTATED"

long = pytae.long
assert long is not None

assert callable(pytae.mutate)
assert hasattr(__import__("pandas").DataFrame, "pt")
assert not hasattr(__import__("pandas").DataFrame, "mutate")

Plotter = pytae.Plotter
assert "pytae.plotting" in sys.modules
assert Plotter is not None
"""
        % _SRC
    )
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", code])


def test_cli_import_does_not_load_shape_or_plotting():
    code = (
        r"""
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, %r)
import pytae.cli

assert "pytae.plotting" not in sys.modules
assert "pytae.shape" not in sys.modules
assert callable(__import__("pytae", fromlist=["filter"]).filter)
assert callable(__import__("pytae", fromlist=["select"]).select)
DF = sys.modules["pandas"].DataFrame
assert hasattr(DF, "pt")
assert not hasattr(DF.pt, "qry")
assert not hasattr(DF, "select")
assert not hasattr(DF, "mutate")
"""
        % _SRC
    )
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", code])


def test_plotter_import_error_mentions_plot_extra():
    code = (
        r"""
import builtins
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, %r)
real_import = builtins.__import__

def blocked(name, *args, **kwargs):
    if name == "matplotlib" or name.startswith("matplotlib."):
        raise ImportError("No module named matplotlib")
    return real_import(name, *args, **kwargs)

builtins.__import__ = blocked
import pytae
try:
    pytae.Plotter
except ImportError as exc:
    msg = str(exc)
    assert "matplotlib" in msg
    assert "pytae[plot]" in msg
else:
    raise AssertionError("expected ImportError")
"""
        % _SRC
    )
    subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-c", code])

# FILE: tests/test_join_concat.py
################################################################################
"""Tests for Pytae library join, concat, and transparent Polars method delegation."""

import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import polars as pl

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

import pytae as pt


def test_df_join_inner_and_chaining():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"], "score": [80, 95, 70]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3, 4], "dept": ["Eng", "HR", "Sales"]})

    # Join and continue chaining Pytae fluent verbs
    res = df1.join(df2, on="id", how="inner").filter("score >= 80").mutate(score_bonus="score + 10").arrange("-score")
    assert isinstance(res, pt.DataFrame)
    assert list(res.columns) == ["id", "name", "score", "dept", "score_bonus"]
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res.iloc[0, "name"] == "Bob"
    assert res.iloc[0, "score_bonus"] == 105


def test_df_join_all_strategies():
    left = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "val": ["a", "b", "c"]})
    right = pt.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3, 4], "score": [20, 30, 40]})

    # left join
    lj = left.join(right, on="id", how="left")
    assert len(lj) == 3
    assert set(lj["id"].to_list()) == {1, 2, 3}

    # right join
    rj = left.join(right, on="id", how="right")
    assert len(rj) == 3
    assert set(rj["id"].to_list()) == {2, 3, 4}

    # full join
    fj = left.join(right, on="id", how="full")
    assert len(fj) == 4
    assert set(fj["id"].to_list()) == {1, 2, 3, 4}

    # semi join (filtering join - returns left rows that match right)
    sj = left.join(right, on="id", how="semi")
    assert len(sj) == 2
    assert list(sj.columns) == ["id", "val"]
    assert set(sj["id"].to_list()) == {2, 3}

    # anti join (returns left rows that do NOT match right)
    aj = left.join(right, on="id", how="anti")
    assert len(aj) == 1
    assert list(aj.columns) == ["id", "val"]
    assert aj.iloc[0, "id"] == 1

    # cross join
    cj = left.join(right, how="cross")
    assert len(cj) == 9  # 3 * 3


def test_df_join_colon_syntax():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "name": ["A", "B", "C"]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"user_id": [2, 3, 4], "role": ["Dev", "PM", "QA"]})

    res = df1.join(df2, on="id:user_id", how="inner")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert "id" in res.columns
    assert "user_id" in res.columns
    assert "role" in res.columns


def test_df_join_auto_detect_common_columns():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"user_id": [1, 2], "score": [90, 85]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"user_id": [2, 3], "grade": ["A", "B"]})

    # Omit on parameter: automatically joins on user_id
    res = df1.join(df2)
    assert len(res) == 1
    assert res.iloc[0, "user_id"] == 2
    assert res.iloc[0, "score"] == 85
    assert res.iloc[0, "grade"] == "A"


def test_top_level_pt_join():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "x": [10, 20]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "y": [200, 300]})

    res = pt.join(df1, df2, on="id", how="left")
    assert isinstance(res, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(res) == 2


def test_pt_accessor_join_pandas_and_polars():
    pdf1 = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": ["a", "b"]})
    pdf2 = pd.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "w": ["x", "y"]})

    # Pandas accessor .pt.join()
    res_pandas = pdf1.pt.join(pdf2, on="id", how="inner")
    assert isinstance(res_pandas, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(res_pandas) == 1
    assert res_pandas.iloc[0, "id"] == 2

    # Polars accessor .pt.join()
    pldf1 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": ["a", "b"]})
    pldf2 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3], "w": ["x", "y"]})
    res_polars = pldf1.pt.join(pldf2, on="id", how="inner")
    assert isinstance(res_polars, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(res_polars) == 1


def test_lazy_join_preserves_lazy_execution():
    lf1 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3], "val": [10, 20, 30]}).lazy()
    lf2 = pl.DataFrame({"id": [2, 3, 4], "bonus": [100, 200, 300]}).lazy()

    df_lazy1 = pt.DataFrame(lf1)
    df_lazy2 = pt.DataFrame(lf2)

    joined_lazy = df_lazy1.join(df_lazy2, on="id", how="inner").filter("val > 10")
    assert joined_lazy.is_lazy

    collected = joined_lazy.collect()
    assert isinstance(collected, pt.DataFrame)
    assert not collected.is_lazy
    assert len(collected) == 2


def test_concat_vertical_and_fallback():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", "y"]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [3, 4], "b": ["w", "z"]})
    df3 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [5, 6], "c": [100, 200]})

    # Top-level concat with matching schemas
    res1 = pt.concat([df1, df2])
    assert len(res1) == 4
    assert list(res1.columns) == ["a", "b"]

    # Method chain concat
    res2 = df1.concat(df2)
    assert len(res2) == 4

    # Top-level concat with differing schemas (diagonal_relaxed fallback)
    res3 = pt.concat([df1, df3])
    assert len(res3) == 4
    assert list(res3.columns) == ["a", "b", "c"]
    assert res3.iloc[0, "c"] is None
    assert res3.iloc[2, "b"] is None


def test_concat_horizontal():
    df1 = pt.DataFrame({"a": [1, 2], "b": ["x", "y"]})
    df2 = pt.DataFrame({"c": [10, 20], "d": [True, False]})

    res = pt.concat([df1, df2], how="horizontal")
    assert len(res) == 2
    assert list(res.columns) == ["a", "b", "c", "d"]


def test_dynamic_polars_forwarding_in_chain():
    df = pt.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2, 3, 4], "amt": [10, 25, 30, 45], "cat": ["a", "b", "a", "b"]})

    # with_columns is a native Polars method!
    # Because of transparent forwarding, it executes and wraps result back into pytae.DataFrame:
    res = (
        df.with_columns(tax=pl.col("amt") * 0.1).filter("tax > 2").by("cat").mutate(total="sum(amt)").arrange("-total")
    )
    assert isinstance(res, pt.DataFrame)
    assert "tax" in res.columns
    assert "total" in res.columns

    # Native slice method
    sliced = df.slice(1, 2)
    assert isinstance(sliced, pt.DataFrame)
    assert len(sliced) == 2

    # Native describe method
    desc = df.describe()
    assert isinstance(desc, pt.DataFrame)
    assert "statistic" in desc.columns

    # Non-DataFrame return (scalar)
    n_unique = df.n_unique()
    assert isinstance(n_unique, int)
    assert n_unique == 4

import os
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import polars as pl
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

import pytae as pt


@pytest.fixture
def sample_csv(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    csv_file = tmp_path / "sample.csv"
    csv_file.write_text(
        "id,group,score,comment\n"
        "1,alpha,10.5,good\n"
        "2,beta,20.0,better\n"
        "3,alpha,15.5,best\n"
        "4,beta,30.0,great\n"
        "5,alpha,,missing\n",
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    return csv_file


@pytest.fixture
def sample_parquet(tmp_path: Path) -> Path:
    pq_file = tmp_path / "sample.parquet"
    df = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "id": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
            "category": ["A", "B", "A", "B", "C"],
            "val1": [10, 20, 30, 40, 50],
            "val2": [100.0, 200.0, 300.0, 400.0, 500.0],
        }
    )
    df.write_parquet(pq_file)
    return pq_file


def test_scan_csv(sample_csv: Path):
    df = pt.scan_csv(sample_csv)
    assert df.is_lazy
    assert "id" in df.columns
    assert "score" in df.columns
    assert df.shape == (5, 4)

    # Chaining preserves laziness
    filtered = df.filter("score > 12")
    assert filtered.is_lazy

    mutated = filtered.mutate(doubled="score * 2")
    assert mutated.is_lazy

    arranged = mutated.arrange("-doubled")
    assert arranged.is_lazy

    selected = arranged.select("id", "group", "doubled")
    assert selected.is_lazy

    # Materialize
    collected = selected.collect()
    assert not collected.is_lazy
    assert list(collected.columns) == ["id", "group", "doubled"]
    assert len(collected) == 3
    assert collected["doubled"].to_list() == [60.0, 40.0, 31.0]


def test_scan_parquet(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet)
    assert df.is_lazy
    assert df.columns == ["id", "category", "val1", "val2"]
    assert df.shape == (5, 4)
    assert len(df) == 5

    res = (
        df.filter("category in ['A', 'B']")
        .mutate(total="val1 + val2")
        .arrange("total desc")
        .select("id", "total")
        .collect()
    )
    assert not res.is_lazy
    assert len(res) == 4
    assert res["total"].to_list() == [440.0, 330.0, 220.0, 110.0]


def test_lazy_explain(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet).filter("val1 > 20").select("id", "category")
    assert df.is_lazy
    explanation = df.explain()
    assert isinstance(explanation, str)
    assert "FILTER" in explanation or "SELECT" in explanation or "val1" in explanation


def test_lazy_conversion():
    eager_df = pt.DataFrame({"x": [1, 2, 3], "y": [4, 5, 6]})
    assert not eager_df.is_lazy

    lazy_df = eager_df.lazy()
    assert lazy_df.is_lazy

    # Collecting returns eager pt.DataFrame
    back = lazy_df.collect()
    assert not back.is_lazy
    assert back["x"].to_list() == [1, 2, 3]


def test_lazy_verbs(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet)

    # distinct
    d = df.distinct("category")
    assert d.is_lazy
    assert len(d.collect()) == 3

    # dropna (Option B zero data loss: bare defaults to how='all', targeted to how='any')
    assert len(df.dropna().collect()) == 5
    assert len(df.drop_nulls().collect()) == 5
    assert len(df.drop_na().collect()) == 5

    dn = df.dropna("val1")
    assert dn.is_lazy
    assert len(dn.collect()) == 5
    assert len(df.drop_nulls("val1").collect()) == 5
    assert len(df.drop_na("val1").collect()) == 5
    assert len(df.dropna(how="any").collect()) == 5

    # pick
    p = df.pick("val1", n=2, order="max")
    assert p.is_lazy
    assert len(p.collect()) == 2
    assert p.collect()["val1"].to_list() == [50, 40]

    # replace_values
    rv = df.replace_values({"A": "ALPHA"}, c="category")
    assert rv.is_lazy
    cats = rv.collect()["category"].to_list()
    assert "ALPHA" in cats
    assert "A" not in cats

    # clean_columns
    cc = df.clean_columns(case="upper")
    assert cc.is_lazy
    assert "CATEGORY" in cc.collect().columns


def test_lazy_grouped_operations(sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet)

    # Grouped mutate on LazyFrame
    g_mut = df.by("category").mutate(mean_val1="mean(val1)")
    assert g_mut.is_lazy
    collected_mut = g_mut.collect()
    assert "mean_val1" in collected_mut.columns

    # Grouped agg on LazyFrame
    g_agg = df.by("category").agg(sum_val1="val1:sum", mean_val2="val2:mean")
    assert g_agg.is_lazy
    collected_agg = g_agg.collect()
    assert "sum_val1" in collected_agg.columns
    assert "mean_val2" in collected_agg.columns
    assert len(collected_agg) == 3


def test_lazy_sinking(tmp_path: Path, sample_parquet: Path):
    df = pt.scan_parquet(sample_parquet).filter("val1 >= 30")
    assert df.is_lazy

    out_pq = tmp_path / "output.parquet"
    df.to_parquet(out_pq)
    assert out_pq.exists()
    assert len(pl.read_parquet(out_pq)) == 3

    out_csv = tmp_path / "output.csv"
    df.to_csv(out_csv)
    assert out_csv.exists()
    assert len(pl.read_csv(out_csv)) == 3


def test_cli_lazy_execution(sample_parquet: Path, tmp_path: Path):
    out_file = tmp_path / "cli_out.csv"
    # Run CLI using python module
    cmd = [
        sys.executable,
        "-m",
        "pytae",
        str(sample_parquet),
        "-filter",
        "val1 > 15",
        "-mutate",
        "calc = val1 * 10",
        "-select",
        "id, calc",
        "-o",
        str(out_file),
    ]
    import subprocess

    subprocess.check_call(cmd)
    assert out_file.exists()
    res = pl.read_csv(out_file)
    assert list(res.columns) == ["id", "calc"]
    assert len(res) == 4
    assert res["calc"].to_list() == [200, 300, 400, 500]


def test_read_and_scan_deprecation():
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="pt.read\\(\\) has been removed; use pt.read_parquet"):
        pt.read("some_file.parquet")

    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="pt.scan\\(\\) has been removed; use pt.scan_parquet"):
        pt.scan("some_file.parquet")


def test_lazy_fillna():
    ldf = pl.LazyFrame({"x": [1.0, float("nan"), None], "y": ["A", None, "B"]})
    df = pt.DataFrame(ldf)
    assert df.is_lazy

    filled = df.fillna(0.0)
    assert filled.is_lazy
    collected = filled.collect()
    assert collected["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    assert collected["y"].to_list() == ["A", None, "B"]

    # Dict fill on lazy frame
    d_filled = df.fillna({"x": 99.0, "y": "MISSING"})
    assert d_filled.is_lazy
    c2 = d_filled.collect()
    assert c2["x"].to_list() == [1.0, 99.0, 99.0]
    assert c2["y"].to_list() == ["A", "MISSING", "B"]

################################################################################
# FILE: tests/test_mutate.py

import os
import sys

import pandas as pd
import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "../src")))

import pytae as pt
from pytae.mutate import parse_mutate_spec


def _df():
    return pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo"],
            "body_mass_g": [3000.0, 4000.0],
            "bill_length_mm": [30.0, 40.0],
        }
    )


def test_mutate_basic_expression():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), bmi="body_mass_g / bill_length_mm ** 2")
    assert list(result["bmi"]) == [pytest.approx(3.333333, rel=1e-4), pytest.approx(2.5)]


def test_mutate_multiple_entries_in_one_call():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), heavy="body_mass_g > 3500", mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000")
    assert list(result["heavy"]) == [False, True]
    assert list(result["mass_kg"]) == [3.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_later_entry_references_earlier_one():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000", mass_lb="mass_kg * 2.20462")
    assert result["mass_lb"].iloc[0] == pytest.approx(6.61386)


def test_mutate_string_comparison_needs_quotes():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), is_adelie="species == 'Adelie'")
    assert list(result["is_adelie"]) == [True, False]


def test_mutate_does_not_modify_original():
    df = _df()
    pt.mutate(df, bmi="body_mass_g / bill_length_mm ** 2")
    assert "bmi" not in df.columns


def test_mutate_overwrites_existing_column():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), body_mass_g="body_mass_g / 1000")
    assert list(result["body_mass_g"]) == [3.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_unknown_column_suggests_typo():
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="did you mean 'body_mass_g'"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), bmi="bod_mass_g / bill_length_mm")


def test_mutate_quoting_column_reference_breaks_arithmetic():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        pt.mutate(_df(), bmi="'body_mass_g' / 'bill_length_mm' ** 2")


def test_mutate_empty_spec_errors():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="mutate\\(\\) expects at least one"):
        pt.mutate(_df())


def test_mutate_if_else_basic():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), size="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy', 'light')")
    assert list(result["size"]) == ["light", "heavy"]


def test_mutate_if_else_numeric_values():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), bonus="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 100, 10)")
    assert list(result["bonus"]) == [10, 100]


def test_mutate_if_else_value_can_be_column_expression():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), adjusted="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, body_mass_g / 1000, body_mass_g)")
    assert list(result["adjusted"]) == [3000.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_if_else_wrong_arg_count_errors():
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        pt.mutate(_df(), size="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy')")


def test_mutate_if_else_mixed_dtype_branches():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), g="if_else(body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy', 0)")
    assert list(result["g"]) in ([0, "heavy"], ["0", "heavy"])


def test_mutate_case_when_mixed_dtype_choices():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), g="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3500, 'heavy'), 0)")
    assert list(result["g"]) in ([0, "heavy"], ["0", "heavy"])


def test_mutate_case_when_first_match_wins():
    result = pt.mutate(
        _df(),
        grade="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A'), (body_mass_g >= 3200, 'B'), 'C')",
    )
    assert list(result["grade"]) == ["C", "A"]


def test_mutate_case_when_no_default_gives_nan_for_unmatched():
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), grade="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A'))")
    assert result["grade"].iloc[1] == "A"
    assert pd.isna(result["grade"].iloc[0])


def test_mutate_case_when_default_must_be_last():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="case_when default .*must be the last argument"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), grade="case_when('C', (body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A'))")


def test_mutate_case_when_requires_at_least_one_entry():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="case_when expects at least one"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), grade="case_when()")


def test_mutate_if_else_and_case_when_chain_with_other_entries():
    result = pt.mutate(
        _df(),
        mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000",
        size="if_else(mass_kg >= 3.5, 'heavy', 'light')",
    )
    assert list(result["size"]) == ["light", "heavy"]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference():
    threshold = 3500.0
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), heavy="body_mass_g >= @threshold")
    assert list(result["heavy"]) == [False, True]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference_via_accessor():
    threshold = 3500.0
    result = _df().pt.mutate(heavy="body_mass_g >= @threshold")
    assert list(result["heavy"]) == [False, True]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference_in_if_else():
    threshold = 3500.0
    result = pt.mutate(_df(), size="if_else(body_mass_g >= @threshold, 'heavy', 'light')")
    assert list(result["size"]) == ["light", "heavy"]


def test_mutate_local_var_reference_in_case_when():
    low, high = 3200.0, 3800.0
    result = pt.mutate(
        _df(),
        grade="case_when((body_mass_g >= @high, 'A'), (body_mass_g >= @low, 'B'), 'C')",
    )
    assert list(result["grade"]) == ["C", "A"]


def test_mutate_unknown_local_var_suggests_typo_free_error():
    with pytest.raises(KeyError, match="threshol"):
        pt.mutate(_df(), heavy="body_mass_g >= @threshol")


def test_mutate_kwargs():
    df = _df()
    res = pt.mutate(df, bmi="body_mass_g / bill_length_mm ** 2", mass_kg="body_mass_g / 1000")
    assert "bmi" in res.columns
    assert "mass_kg" in res.columns
    assert list(res["mass_kg"]) == [3.0, 4.0]


def test_mutate_rejects_unsupported_positional_types():
    df = _df()
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="unexpected positional argument"):
        df.pt.mutate(123)
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="unexpected positional argument"):
        df.pt.mutate([1, 2, 3])
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="callables as keyword arguments"):
        df.pt.mutate(lambda d: d)


def test_mutate_callable_lambda():
    df = _df()
    res = pt.mutate(df, bmi=lambda d: d["body_mass_g"] / d["bill_length_mm"] ** 2)
    assert "bmi" in res.columns
    assert list(res["bmi"]) == [pytest.approx(3.333333, rel=1e-4), pytest.approx(2.5)]


def test_mutate_constants():
    df = _df()
    res = pt.mutate(df, status="'active'", count=42)
    assert list(res["status"]) == ["active", "active"]
    assert list(res["count"]) == [42, 42]


def test_mutate_case_when_default_kwarg():
    df = _df()
    res = pt.mutate(df, g="case_when((body_mass_g >= 3500, 'A'), default='B')")
    assert list(res["g"]) == ["B", "A"]


def test_mutate_case_when_flat_alternating_pairs():
    df = _df()
    res = pt.mutate(df, g="case_when(body_mass_g >= 3800, 'A', body_mass_g >= 3200, 'B', default='C')")
    assert list(res["g"]) == ["C", "A"]


def test_mutate_coalesce_helper():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1.0, None, None], "b": [None, 2.0, None]})
    res = pt.mutate(df, c="coalesce(a, b, 0.0)")
    assert list(res["c"]) == [1.0, 2.0, 0.0]


def test_mutate_bracketed_and_backtick_columns_in_fallback():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"col a": [10, 20], "col b": [1, 2]})
    res1 = pt.mutate(df, c="if_else([col a] > 15, 'high', 'low')")
    assert list(res1["c"]) == ["low", "high"]
    res2 = pt.mutate(df, c="if_else(`col a` > 15, 'high', 'low')")
    assert list(res2["c"]) == ["low", "high"]
    res3 = pt.mutate(df, total="[col a] + [col b]")
    assert list(res3["total"]) == [11, 22]


def test_parse_mutate_spec_equals_and_comments():
    spec = """
    # calculate weight in kg
    mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000
    # calculate weight in lbs
    mass_lb = mass_kg * 2.2
    """
    res = parse_mutate_spec(spec)
    assert "mass_kg" in res
    assert "mass_lb" in res
    assert res["mass_kg"] == "body_mass_g / 1000"


def test_parse_mutate_spec_rejects_colon():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="use '=' for assignment"):
        parse_mutate_spec("mass_kg: body_mass_g / 1000")


def test_mutate_load_from_file(tmp_path):
    df = _df()
    file_path = tmp_path / "specs.txt"
    file_path.write_text("mass_kg = body_mass_g / 1000\n# comment\nmass_lb = mass_kg * 2.2\n")
    res = pt.mutate(df, f"@{file_path}")
    assert "mass_kg" in res.columns
    assert "mass_lb" in res.columns


def test_mutate_explicit_params():

    assert list(res["flag"]) == [False, True]

    assert "params" in res1.columns
    assert list(res1["params"]) == [10, 10]

def test_mutate_bracketed_columns():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"body mass g": [3000.0, 4000.0], "height": [1.5, 2.0]})
    # Target column has brackets, source has brackets
    res1 = df.pt.mutate("[mass kg] = [body mass g] / 1000")
    assert "mass kg" in res1.columns
    assert list(res1["mass kg"]) == [3.0, 4.0]

    # Mixed source columns (one with space, one without)
    res2 = df.pt.mutate("[bmi score] = [body mass g] / (height ** 2)")
    assert "bmi score" in res2.columns


def test_mutate_grouped_single_col():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [10.0, 20.0, 60.0]})
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate(
        "avg = mean(val), diff = val - avg, total = sum(val), cnt = n, cnt2 = n()",
    )
    assert list(res["avg"]) == [15.0, 15.0, 60.0]
    assert list(res["diff"]) == [-5.0, 5.0, 0.0]
    assert list(res["total"]) == [30.0, 30.0, 60.0]
    assert list(res["cnt"]) == [2, 2, 1]
    assert list(res["cnt2"]) == [2, 2, 1]


def test_mutate_grouped_multi_col():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "g1": ["a", "a", "a", "b"],
            "g2": ["x", "x", "y", "x"],
            "val": [10.0, 30.0, 5.0, 100.0],
        }
    )
    res1 = df.pt.by("g1", "g2").pt.mutate("m = mean(val), cnt = n")
    assert list(res1["m"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 5.0, 100.0]
    assert list(res1["cnt"]) == [2, 2, 1, 1]

    # Positional pt.by with multiple columns
    res2 = pt.mutate(pt.by(df, "g1", "g2"), "m = mean(val)")
    assert list(res2["m"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 5.0, 100.0]


def test_mutate_grouped_spaced_brackets():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"group code": ["a", "a", "b"], "total bill": [10.0, 30.0, 50.0]})
    res = df.pt.by("group code").pt.mutate("[diff bill] = [total bill] - mean([total bill])")
    assert list(res["diff bill"]) == [-10.0, 10.0, 0.0]


def test_mutate_grouped_dropna_observed():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", None, "a"], "val": [10.0, 50.0, 30.0]})
    # Default is dropna=False: computes on the NA group
    res_default = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)")
    assert res_default["m"].iloc[1] == 50.0
    assert res_default["m"].iloc[0] == 20.0
    assert res_default["m"].iloc[2] == 20.0

    res_dropna = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)", dropna=True)
    assert pd.isna(res_dropna["m"].iloc[1])
    assert res_dropna["m"].iloc[0] == 20.0
    assert res_dropna["m"].iloc[2] == 20.0

    res_keepna = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)", dropna=False)
    assert res_keepna["m"].iloc[1] == 50.0


def test_mutate_grouped_duplicate_index():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "b", "a"], "val": [10.0, 50.0, 30.0]}, index=[0, 1, 0])
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("m = mean(val)")
    assert list(res["m"]) == [20.0, 50.0, 20.0]
    assert list(res.index) == [0, 1, 0]


def test_mutate_grouped_functional_and_callable():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [10.0, 20.0, 60.0]})
    # Functional pt.mutate
    res1 = pt.mutate(pt.by(df, "grp"), "avg = mean(val)")
    assert list(res1["avg"]) == [15.0, 15.0, 60.0]

    # Callable inside grouped mutate
    res2 = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate(half_mean=lambda g: g["val"].mean() / 2)
    assert list(res2["half_mean"]) == [7.5, 7.5, 30.0]


def test_mutate_rejects_by_arg():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "b"], "val": [1, 2]})
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="df.pt.mutate\\(\\) does not accept 'by'"):
        df.pt.mutate("m = mean(val)", by="grp")
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="mutate\\(\\) does not accept 'by'"):
        pt.mutate(df, "m = mean(val)", by="grp")


def test_mutate_coalesce_scalar_broadcast():
    # Lib Issue 5
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [None, 2.0, None]}, index=[5, 6, 7])
    res1 = pt.mutate(df, c="coalesce(0, a)")

    res2 = pt.mutate(df, c="coalesce(1, 2)")
    assert list(res2["c"]) == [1, 1, 1]


def test_mutate_column_named_sum_overrides_helper():

    df = pd.DataFrame({"sum": [1, 2], "x": [10, 20]})
    res = df.pt.mutate(y="if_else(x > 15, sum, 0)")
    assert list(res["y"]) == [0, 2]


def test_mutate_map_preserves_explicit_null():
    # Lib Issue 11
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": ["x", "y", "z"]})
    res = pt.mutate(df, b="map(a, {'x': 1, 'y': None}, -1)")
    assert res["b"].iloc[0] == 1.0
    assert pd.isna(res["b"].iloc[1])
    assert res["b"].iloc[2] == -1.0


def test_mutate_if_else_and_case_when_nullable_boolean():
    # Lib Issue 12
    df = pd.DataFrame({"a": pd.Series([1, pd.NA, 3], dtype="Int64")})
    res_if = pt.mutate(df, b="if_else(a > 2, 'y', 'n')")
    assert list(res_if["b"]) == ["n", "n", "y"]

    res_cw = pt.mutate(df, b="case_when((a > 2, 'y'), 'n')")
    assert list(res_cw["b"]) == ["n", "n", "y"]


def test_mutate_n_row_count_vs_col_and_helper():
    # Lib Issue 16: caller local 'n' does not shadow row count 'n' unless referenced as '@n'
    n = 999  # noqa: F841
    df = pd.DataFrame({"val": [10, 20, 30]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("cnt = n, caller_n = @n")
    assert list(res["cnt"]) == [3, 3, 3]
    assert list(res["caller_n"]) == [999, 999, 999]


def test_mutate_grouped_callable_sees_original_index():
    # Lib Issue 17: callable sees original index in grouped mutate
    s = pd.Series([100, 200, 300], index=[10, 20, 30])
    df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "b", "a"], "x": [1, 2, 3]}, index=[10, 20, 30])
    res = df.pt.by("g").pt.mutate(y=lambda d: d["x"] + s.reindex(d.index))
    assert list(res["y"]) == [101, 202, 303]
    assert list(res.index) == [10, 20, 30]


def test_mutate_scalar_if_else_and_case_when():
    # Lib Issue 1 (Review 2ec5bbba): scalar condition in if_else and case_when broadcasts across rows and groups
    df = pd.DataFrame({"val": [10, 20, 30]})
    assert df.pt.mutate(y="if_else(n > 1, 1, 0)")["y"].tolist() == [1, 1, 1]
    assert df.pt.mutate(y="case_when((n > 1, 'big'), 'small')")["y"].tolist() == ["big", "big", "big"]

    df2 = pd.DataFrame({"val": [10, 20, 30]}, index=[5, 6, 7])
    assert df2.pt.mutate(y="if_else(n > 1, 1, 0)")["y"].tolist() == [1, 1, 1]

    df3 = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "a", "b"], "val": [10, 20, 30]})
    assert df3.pt.by("g").pt.mutate(y="if_else(n > 1, 1, 0)")["y"].tolist() == [1, 1, 0]


def test_mutate_lit_constant_when_column_exists():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"original": [10, 20], "val": [1, 2]})

    # Without inner quotes, passing source="original" copies the column
    assert list(df.pt.mutate(source="original")["source"]) == [10, 20]

    # With inner quotes source="'original'", assigns literal string
    res_quoted = df.pt.mutate(source="'original'")
    assert list(res_quoted["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    # Positional string expression with inner quotes
    res_pos = df.pt.mutate("source = 'original'")
    assert list(res_pos["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    # Grouped mutation with quoted literal
    res_grp = df.pt.by("val").pt.mutate(source="'original'")
    assert list(res_grp["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    res_grp_str = df.pt.by("val").pt.mutate("source = 'original'")
    assert list(res_grp_str["source"]) == ["original", "original"]

    # Native Python non-string literals (int, float, bool)
    res_num = df.pt.mutate(source=42, flag=True)
    assert list(res_num["source"]) == [42, 42]
    assert list(res_num["flag"]) == [True, True]

    # Calling pt.lit() raises AttributeError pointing to quoted syntax
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError, match="pt.lit\\(\\) has been removed"):
        pt.lit("original")


def test_mutate_grouped_vectorized_all_stats():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "grp": ["a", "a", "a", "b", "b"],
            "val": [10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 100.0, 200.0],
            "name": ["alice", "bob", "charlie", "dave", "eve"],
        }
    )
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate(
        "avg = mean(val), tot = sum(val), med = median(val), "
        "lo = min(val), hi = max(val), sd = std(val), vr = var(val), "
        "cnt = n, cnt_fn = n(), upper_name = name.str.upper()"
    )
    assert list(res["avg"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 150.0, 150.0]
    assert list(res["tot"]) == [60.0, 60.0, 60.0, 300.0, 300.0]
    assert list(res["med"]) == [20.0, 20.0, 20.0, 150.0, 150.0]
    assert list(res["lo"]) == [10.0, 10.0, 10.0, 100.0, 100.0]
    assert list(res["hi"]) == [30.0, 30.0, 30.0, 200.0, 200.0]
    assert list(res["cnt"]) == [3, 3, 3, 2, 2]
    assert list(res["cnt_fn"]) == [3, 3, 3, 2, 2]
    assert list(res["upper_name"]) == ["ALICE", "BOB", "CHARLIE", "DAVE", "EVE"]


def test_mutate_grouped_fallback_series_method():
    # Expressions calling custom Series methods like .cumsum() fall back to per-group evaluation
    df = pd.DataFrame({"grp": ["a", "a", "b", "b"], "val": [1, 2, 10, 20]})
    res = df.pt.by("grp").pt.mutate("cs = val.cumsum()")
    assert list(res["cs"]) == [1, 3, 10, 30]


def test_mutate_multi_col_in_place_and_chaining():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"rev": [100.0, 200.0], "cost": [40.0, 80.0], "tax": [10.0, 20.0]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("(rev, cost, tax) = _ * 1.5, profit = rev - cost - tax")
    assert list(res["rev"]) == [150.0, 300.0]
    assert list(res["cost"]) == [60.0, 120.0]
    assert list(res["tax"]) == [15.0, 30.0]
    assert list(res["profit"]) == [75.0, 150.0]


def test_mutate_multi_col_suffix_and_prefix():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"rev": [100.0, 200.0], "cost": [50.0, 100.0]})
    res_suf = df.pt.mutate("(rev, cost)_usd = _ * 1.08")
    assert list(res_suf["rev"]) == [100.0, 200.0]
    assert list(res_suf["rev_usd"]) == [pytest.approx(108.0), pytest.approx(216.0)]
    assert list(res_suf["cost_usd"]) == [pytest.approx(54.0), pytest.approx(108.0)]

    res_pre = df.pt.mutate("norm_(rev, cost) = _ / max(_)")
    assert list(res_pre["norm_rev"]) == [0.5, 1.0]
    assert list(res_pre["norm_cost"]) == [0.5, 1.0]


def test_mutate_multi_col_selectors_and_grouped():
    df = pd.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["Adelie", "Adelie", "Gentoo", "Gentoo"],
            "bill_length_mm": [30.0, 50.0, 40.0, 60.0],
            "bill_depth_mm": [10.0, 20.0, 15.0, 25.0],
        }
    )
    res_sw = df.pt.mutate("(startswith=bill_) = _ / 10")
    assert list(res_sw["bill_length_mm"]) == [3.0, 5.0, 4.0, 6.0]
    assert list(res_sw["bill_depth_mm"]) == [1.0, 2.0, 1.5, 2.5]

    # Grouped dtype=numeric selector (automatically excludes grouping columns)
    res_grp = df.pt.by("species").pt.mutate("(dtype=numeric) = _ - mean(_)")
    assert list(res_grp["bill_length_mm"]) == [-10.0, 10.0, -10.0, 10.0]
    assert list(res_grp["bill_depth_mm"]) == [-5.0, 5.0, -5.0, 5.0]


def test_mutate_multi_col_spaced_columns():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"col a": [10, 20], "col b": [30, 40]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("([col a], [col b]) = _ + 5")
    assert list(res["col a"]) == [15, 25]
    assert list(res["col b"]) == [35, 45]


def test_mutate_map_with_spaced_columns():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"island name": ["Biscoe", "Dream", "Torgersen"]})
    res = df.pt.mutate("[island code] = map([island name], {'Biscoe': 'BIS', 'Dream': 'DRM'}, 'TOR')")
    assert list(res["island code"]) == ["BIS", "DRM", "TOR"]


def test_mutate_disallow_dot_map_method_syntax():
    df = pd.DataFrame({"species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo"], "island name": ["Biscoe", "Dream"]})
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="'.map\\(\\)' method syntax is not supported"):
        df.pt.mutate("code = species.map({'Adelie': 'AD'})")

    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="'.map\\(\\)' method syntax is not supported"):
        df.pt.mutate("[code] = [island name].map({'Biscoe': 'BIS'})")


def test_mutate_map_column_and_expr_defaults():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "species": ["Adelie", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"],
            "alt_name": ["Penguin A", "Penguin G", "Penguin C"],
        }
    )
    # 1. Fallback to column itself (preserves unmapped values)
    r1 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'}, species)")
    assert list(r1["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]

    # 2. 2-argument map (unmapped values become null)
    r2 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'})")
    assert list(r2["mapped"]) == ["AD", None, None]

    # 3. Fallback to another column
    r3 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'}, alt_name)")
    assert list(r3["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Penguin G", "Penguin C"]

    # 4. Keyword default=...
    r4 = df.mutate(mapped="map(species, {'Adelie': 'AD'}, default=species)")
    assert list(r4["mapped"]) == ["AD", "Gentoo", "Chinstrap"]


def test_mutate_smart_fillna_and_fill_null_fill_nan():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [1.0, float("nan"), None],
            "str_col": ["alpha", None, "gamma"],
        }
    )

    # 1. fillna(col, val) -> fills both NaN and null by default (nans=True)
    r1 = df.mutate(clean="fillna(flt, 0.0)")
    assert list(r1["clean"]) == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 2. fillna(col, val, nans=False) -> fills null only, leaves NaN intact
    r2 = df.mutate(clean="fillna(flt, 0.0, nans=False)")
    assert r2["clean"][0] == 1.0 and str(r2["clean"][1]) == "nan" and r2["clean"][2] == 0.0

    # 3. fill_null(col, val) -> strict null filling
    r3 = df.mutate(clean="fill_null(flt, 0.0)")
    assert r3["clean"][0] == 1.0 and str(r3["clean"][1]) == "nan" and r3["clean"][2] == 0.0

    # 4. fill_nan(col, val) -> strict NaN filling
    r4 = df.mutate(clean="fill_nan(flt, 0.0)")
    assert r4["clean"][0] == 1.0 and r4["clean"][1] == 0.0 and r4["clean"][2] is None

    # 5. Method syntax col.fillna(0.0)
    r5 = df.mutate(clean="flt.fillna(0.0)")
    assert list(r5["clean"]) == [1.0, 0.0, 0.0]

    # 6. fillna on string column (safely fills null without is_nan error)
    r6 = df.mutate(clean="fillna(str_col, 'MISSING')")
    assert list(r6["clean"]) == ["alpha", "MISSING", "gamma"]

    # 7. Method syntax str_col.fill_null('MISSING')
    r7 = df.mutate(clean="str_col.fill_null('MISSING')")
    assert list(r7["clean"]) == ["alpha", "MISSING", "gamma"]


def test_handle_missing_cleans_float_nans():
    df = pt.DataFrame(
        {
            "flt": [10.0, float("nan"), None, 30.0],
        }
    )
    # numeric_fill=0 fills both NaN and null
    cleaned = df.handle_missing(numeric_fill=0)
    assert list(cleaned["flt"]) == [10.0, 0.0, 0.0, 30.0]

    # numeric_fill="mean" computes mean ignoring NaNs and nulls (mean of 10 and 30 is 20)
    cleaned_mean = df.handle_missing(numeric_fill="mean")
    assert list(cleaned_mean["flt"]) == [10.0, 20.0, 20.0, 30.0]
